findings.title: False accumulated rounding bound in Proposition 4.13 proof
findings.status: demonstrated invalid core derivation; local replacement proved
findings.source_locator: pp.49–50 Proposition4.13 proof; definitions pp.16–17 and48
findings.hypotheses: q∈(0,1),t>0,finite skew partitions λ/μ,ν/ρ, λ1≤at,ν1≤a't; coordinatewise floor/ceiling
findings.evidence: q=1/2,t=2,γ=1,λ=μ=empty,ν=(2,2,2),ρ=(1,1,1),a=0,a'=1; unique ceiling Schur maximizer has Δ=3/2>1. Arbitrarily large t family m=ceil(t^3) defeats uniform vanishing error.
findings.proof: reports/0511.tex Problem1: exact weight product P(A+)P(A−)≥P(λ/μ)P(ν/ρ) yields stronger midpoint inequality with ε=0
findings.counterevidence: This repair proves the intermediate proposition; no counterexample to final lower-tail theorem. Arbitrary configurations do not necessarily maximize the supremum.
findings.repair_scope: Exact midpoint inequality for all t>0,a,a'≥0; infinite right side handles negative input; not certification of remaining variational/deconvolution proof.

findings.title: Missing lattice phase in normalized Bessel asymptotic
findings.status: false assertion demonstrated analytically; needed local trace estimate repaired
findings.source_locator: p.24 Lemma3.4 eq.(3.14); application pp.29–30 eq.(3.30)
findings.hypotheses: fixed u>2, real t→∞; n=floor(ut); Bessel Jn(2t)
findings.evidence: u=3,t=n/3 and t=(n+1/2)/3 yield distinct limits1 and(3+sqrt5)/2. Own contour saddle proof retains r=n/t.
findings.counterevidence: Integer-ut subsequence does have limit1; bounded positive phase does not alter speed-t rate. Corrected saddle formula restores local lower bound.
findings.core_dependency: Eq.(3.14) directly used in Proposition3.2 trace lower bound underpinning Theorem3.1/upper-tail argument.
findings.repair_scope: Replace u by n/t in normalized asymptotic, or include exp(Phi+'(u){ut}); also use p floor(u*t)−tPhi+(u*)≥tΥ(p)−p. Remainder Fredholm analysis not independently certified.

findings.title: Lemma3.7 diverges at permitted endpoint v=0

findings.evidence: r=.5,γ1=3,γ2=4,v=0,t=1; a=j+.5,ℓ=2.5−j repeats J3(2)^2 infinitely. Alternating series J3(2)>1/8 gives divergence.
